simple.meaning: אֵת (ʼêth) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a hoe or other digging implement.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across 1 Samuel, Isaiah, Joel, Micah, beginning at 1 Samuel 13:20. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵת (H855).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אֵת (ʼêth) / H855 is traced through 1 Samuel 13:20, 1 Samuel 13:21, Isaiah 2:4, Joel 4:10 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: a hoe or other digging implement

firstOccurrence.englishText: but all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his own plowshare, mattock, ax, and sickle.

timeline.evidenceText: but all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his own plowshare, mattock, ax, and sickle.
The price was one payim† A payim (or pim) was 2/3 shekel of silver, or 0.26 ounces, or 7.6 grams each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
He will judge between the nations,
and he will judge between many peoples,

definitions.full: H855. eth III. אֵת see אתת . אַתְּי אַתְּ, אַתָּה, see below אנת . III. [ אֵת ] noun [masculine] a cutting instrument of iron usually transl . ploughshare — singular suffix אֵתוֺ 1Sam 13:20 ; plural אֵתִים 13:21 , אִתִּים Isa 2:4 = Micah 4:3 ; suffix אִתֵּיכֶם Joel 4:10; according to Klo and others also 2Kin 6:5 אֶתהַֿבַּרְזֶל , i.e. the axe of iron.
